basis: Congenital diaphragm and upper-limb structural defects; frequency of associated pulmonary hypoplasia is not established for this syndrome.
Intellectual disability, movement disorder, deafness and ophthalmoplegia define the syndrome; renal abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.
Joubert neurodevelopmental disorder; strabismus and ptosis in 4/4, and structural hand polydactyly in 4/4; hearing loss only 1/4.
Primary carcinoma arising from hepatocytes; underlying viral hepatitis or cirrhosis is a separate disease.
Hereditary essential tremor is a neurologic movement disorder; vocal tremor does not establish airway damage.
Familial myoclonic epilepsy with cortical myoclonic tremor; no established direct extra-neurologic damage.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; scoliosis in 2/3 and structural foot deformities in 2/4; cataract in 1/2 assessed patients. Small denominators limit certainty.
Sustained atrial rhythm disorder; stroke and heart failure are separately diagnosed complications.
Terminal complement deficiency is an immunodeficiency; meningococcal or gonococcal infections are separate diseases.
Developmental delay, intellectual disability and obesity define the syndrome; ocular abnormalities and reflux are only occasional.
Immune-mediated Guillain-Barre variant directly damages motor and sensory axons; respiratory weakness reflects neural dysfunction.
Vitreoretinal B-cell lymphoma; direct CNS involvement by the same lymphoma develops in roughly 50-80% over its course.
Primary lung adenocarcinoma detected by sputum cytology despite an unlocalizable primary tumor.
Pancreatic endocrine tumor; small-intestinal neoplasm annotation does not establish spread of this tumor. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver damage.
Inherited LDL metabolism disorder; very frequent atherosclerosis and frequent hepatic steatosis are separately diagnosed diseases, excluded under rule 3.
Cartilaginous or associated soft-tissue sarcoma with myxoid changes; no common extra-organ occupation established.
Skeletal muscle channelopathy causing myotonia; cardiac abnormalities and dysphagia are very rare, not defining manifestations.
ID, skeletal defects and oral clefting define it; corneal opacity/microphthalmia in 1/2. Hearing loss and septal abnormality, each 1/2, omitted by cap.
Benign or malignant neoplasm arising in skin; subtype-specific origins or spread do not apply across the umbrella.
Tetrahydrobiopterin synthesis disorder causing neurotransmitter deficiency, dystonia and motor delay, even with minimal hyperphenylalaninemia.
Chronic T-cell-mediated inflammatory skin disorder; possible progression to cutaneous lymphoma is a separate disease, not additional involvement.
Primary microcephaly; atrial septal defect and tracheal stenosis each 2/2; cleft soft palate 1/2. Finger malformation omitted by cap; very small cohort.
Mature T-cell lymphoma arising in and infiltrating intestinal epithelium.
Lesch-Nyhan-like neurologic syndrome with hyperuricemia despite normal HGPRT; no evidence of common direct renal damage.
Congenital cerebral cortical malformation causing common developmental impairment, seizures and hemiparesis; no additional organ damage established.
